items.title: /forgot-password and /resend-verification have no rate limit — mailbomb / token-clobber
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth.rs:1461 — check_rate_limit is only invoked on /login (line 555). /forgot-password and /resend-verification generate + persist a token and enqueue an email on every request with NO per-email, per-IP, or global throttle. Attacker who knows a target email can mailbomb their inbox (phishing amplification) and burn the org's email-service quota. The intentional generic response also means there's no feedback loop to detect abuse. And because every hit invalidates prior tokens, a bystander who knows the email can break an in-flight password reset.

items.title: SECURITY: Alexa voice webhook accepts forged requests — verify_alexa_signature never checks the signature
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:750 — verify_alexa_signature() binds the Signature header to `_signature` and never uses it. It validates only the SignatureCertChainUrl format (validate_alexa_cert_url) and the body timestamp (validate_alexa_timestamp), then returns Ok(()). The in-code comment admits steps 3 & 4 (fetch cert chain, verify signature with the cert public key) are unimplemented.

Reachable and stateful: voice_webhook_router() is mounted at lib.rs:340 under /api/v1/webhooks/voice, and alexa_webhook (voice_webhooks.rs:95) takes an `RlsConnection` — so a forged request reaches tenant data.

Exploit shape: POST /api/v1/webhooks/voice/alexa with SignatureCertChainUrl=https://s3.amazonaws.com/echo.api/x, any non-empty Signature header, and a body timestamp inside the 150s window is accepted as an authentic Alexa delivery.
Secondary: the /verify helper endpoint (voice_webhooks.rs:698) reports alexa signatures as `valid: !request.signature.is_empty()` — a self-described 'simplified check for demo'.

Fix direction: mirror the repo's existing hardened webhook convention (routes/portal_webhooks.rs::verify_timestamped_portal_webhook, routes/layout/webhook.rs::sign_timestamped_payload) or add real x509 chain validation via x509-parser; until then the route should fail closed.

evidence: .github/workflows/api-validation.yml triggers only on `docs/api/**` (push and pull_request). The `generate-sdks` drift gate that compares the committed frontend/packages/api-client/src/generated tree against a fresh openapi-ts run was added 2026-07-22 in PR #2444 (7e982cf91).
docs/api/** has not changed on dev since 902110d (2026-07-19), so the gate has NEVER executed on dev with the gate present — the last green dev run predates it.

Both api-validation runs since the gate landed failed: 2026-07-23 (auto-impl/refactor-churn-hotspot-ppt-dashboard-md-1efc81ca) and 2026-07-28 (auto-impl/refactor-churn-hotspot-repo-map-md-2026-5bfbe482, run 30399201262). The failure is real committed drift — the artifact downloaded and verified its digest cleanly; the regenerated client differs from the committed one by a large export-type set.
Consequence 1: dev ships an @ppt/api-client that does not match docs/api/typespec, and no scheduled or dev-push run can catch it.

Consequence 2: unrelated docs-only PRs inherit a red required check they did not cause — currently blocking PR #2482 (a docs/repo-map.md-only change). A force-push that re-bases such a branch widens the push-event path comparison enough to trip the docs/api/** filter.

Fix direction: (a) regenerate and commit the client in its own PR to clear the standing drift, and (b) widen the trigger so the gate actually guards — add frontend/packages/api-client/** to the paths, or run generate-sdks on every push to dev (it needs the validate job's openapi-spec artifact, so keep the job dependency).
Note the workflow's own comment: @ppt/reality-api-client is explicitly NOT gated (older generator template set) — that carve-out compounds the blind spot.

items.title: mobile: useOfflineSupport — transient (5xx/network) queued actions are permanently DROPPED after 3 retries with only console.error — silent loss of offline-created content

frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:399-401 — carriedForward = queue.filter(a => !succeededIds.has(a.id) && !terminalFailureIds.has(a.id)); anything in terminalFailureIds is excluded from `merged` and thus deleted from QUEUE_KEY on the subsequent AsyncStorage.setItem. frontend/apps/mobile/src/App.tsx:81-83,337 — the sync-toast's only recovery is onRetry={handleRetrySync} which just calls processQueue() again. Because the terminally-dropped action is no longer in the queue, tapping Retry cannot recover it. For queued fault reports/meter readings/votes/acknowledgements made while offline this is silent data loss after transient server unavailability.
Fix: treat only isPermanent (4xx) as terminal; give transient failures a larger bounded budget or move them to a dead-letter store surfaced in the UI rather than deleting them.

routes/lazyRoutes.tsx defines ~90 `lazy(() => import(...))` page chunks. A rejected dynamic import is NOT caught by Suspense — it propagates as a thrown error. After a redeploy, a user holding a stale index.html requests an old hashed chunk that no longer exists on the CDN (404) — a routine production event for a Vite hashed-chunk SPA. That rejection, or any render-time throw inside a page, bubbles to the ROOT boundary and unmounts the entire application shell.

components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:99 handleRetry only resets `hasError` and re-renders — for a failed lazy() import the browser has permanently cached the rejected module promise, so 'Try Again' re-throws immediately; only 'Reload Page' (window.location.reload, :182) recovers.

Fix: wrap `<Suspense><AppRoutes/></Suspense>` in App.tsx:229 with a route-scoped `<ErrorBoundary>` (component supports a custom `fallback`) so failures are contained to the `<main>` outlet, keeping AppNavigation/shell mounted. items.title: mobile-rn: the cold-start initialize() effect reads the stored access token (SecureSto...
evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:85-95 — the cold-start `initialize()` effect reads the stored access token (`SecureStore.getItemAsync(ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY)`) and, whenever both `accessToken` and `userJson` are present, unconditionally sets `{ isLoading:false, isAuthenticated:true, user, accessToken }`. It never decodes/checks the token's `exp` claim and never calls the existing `refreshToken()`. Because access tokens are short-lived (refresh tokens are the long-lived credential — see REFRESH_TOKEN_KEY / the /auth/refresh flow at :209-231), any app cold-start that happens after the stored access token's TTL has elapsed restores the user into an `isAuthenticated:true` state holding an already-expired bearer token.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:296-312 — `authenticateWithBiometric` has the identical gap on the unlock path: after `LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync` succeeds it reads the stored `accessToken`/`userJson` and sets `isAuthenticated:true` with that token, with an explicit comment (":296") that it deliberately does NOT refetch/reset (issue #2399) — but it also performs no `exp` validation and no proactive `refreshToken()`, so a biometric unlock after the access token expired lands the user authenticated-but-with-an-expired-token.

This compounds the already-filed `code-review-mobile-rn-useapi-no-refresh-retry` (the API layer does not transparently refresh + retry on 401): with no proactive refresh at restore/unlock AND no reactive refresh-retry in useApi, the first request after an expired restore 401s and the user is stuck in a broken 'logged in but everything fails' state until a manual logout/login. `refreshToken()` already exists in this same context (:209) and is simply never invoked on the two restore paths. Fix: on `initialize()` and on successful biometric unlock, decode the access token's `exp` (utils/jwt.ts already ships a guarded `decodeJwtPayload`) and, if expired/near-expiry, `await refreshToken()` before setting `isAuthenticated:true` (fall back to the login screen if refresh fails).

items.title: ppt-web-core: the client heartbeat sends an APPLICATION-level ping frame {type:'ping', pa...
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:688-709 — the client heartbeat sends an APPLICATION-level ping frame `{type:'ping', payload:null, timestamp}` via send() every heartbeatInterval (default 30000ms, :288), sets `awaitingPong = true`, and arms a pongTimeout (default 10000ms, :289). The ONLY thing that clears awaitingPong is receiving a text frame whose `data.type === 'pong'` (handleMessage :529-532 -> handlePong :711-718). If no such frame arrives within 10s, `this.socket?.close(4000, 'Pong timeout')` fires (:705), producing a non-clean close -> onclose (:495-510) -> scheduleReconnect().

The api-server notification WS handler NEVER sends an application-level `{type:'pong'}`. Verified in backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ws_notifications.rs: the server only emits `Message::Text` carrying the `{event, payload}` WsEvent envelope (:219-230) for notifications, and uses PROTOCOL-level `Message::Ping(vec![])` for its own liveness probe (:242). Its inbound arm (:257-260) explicitly treats every client frame (Text/Binary/Ping/Pong) as a heartbeat and returns without replying — see the module header comment (:27, 'Client -> server: any message is treated as a heartbeat (pong)'). No code path serialises the string 'pong' back to the client.

Consequence: on every connection the client opens (onopen -> startHeartbeat :488-493), 30s later it sends `{type:'ping'}`, the server swallows it, awaitingPong stays true, and at ~40s the client force-closes with code 4000 and reconnects. onclose->stopHeartbeat->scheduleReconnect->connect->onopen->startHeartbeat repeats the cycle indefinitely. parseServerMessage (:59-76) maps real notification events onto `type = <event name>`, never 'pong', so an incoming notification never clears awaitingPong either. The realtime notification channel therefore drops and reconnects roughly every 40s for the entire authenticated session.

Reachability confirmed in production: App.tsx:94-101 mounts <WebSocketProvider> around the whole authenticated app with NO heartbeatInterval/pongTimeout override, so the 30s/10s defaults apply; WebSocketContext.tsx:250-251 calls service.connect() whenever auth.isAuthenticated && accessToken. Impact: constant socket churn, missed pushes during each reconnect gap, redundant server WS-session setup/teardown, and spurious onDisconnected/onReconnected callback firing every ~40s. Fix: the client-side app-level ping is both wrong (server never answers it) and redundant (the server already pings and the browser auto-pongs at the protocol level, invisible to JS). Remove the sendPing/pongTimeout logic and rely on the server's Message::Ping + browser auto-pong for liveness; OR have the server echo an application `{type:'pong'}` on receipt of `{type:'ping'}` so the contract matches. Distinct from the prior ws-token-rotation-stale and ws-ungated-console findings.

items.title: ppt-web-core: once reconnectAttempts reaches maxReconnectAttempts (default 10, :290) sche...
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:600-612 — once reconnectAttempts reaches maxReconnectAttempts (default 10, :290) scheduleReconnect() sets `shouldReconnect = false`, emits `connection:max-retries-exceeded`, and sets an error state. From that point NOTHING in the client re-arms reconnection: onclose only reconnects when shouldReconnect is true (:507), and reconnectAttempts is never reset by connect() or disconnect() — only a successful onopen resets it (:489). The public resetReconnectAttempts() (:479-481) is dead code (no caller in the segment).

The default backoff sum (min 1000ms doubling, capped at 30000ms, over 10 attempts) is only ~3 minutes, so any real outage longer than that — laptop sleep, tunnel/VPN drop, backend redeploy window, mobile network gap — permanently kills the notification socket for the rest of the session.

There is no auto-resume wiring. contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx only calls service.connect() on an auth change (:246-256); it never subscribes to `connection:max-retries-exceeded` and is not connected to hooks/useNetworkStatus.ts (which already detects browser online/offline transitions, useNetworkStatus.ts:96-121). So when connectivity returns, the socket stays dead until the user logs out/in or reloads the page — user silently stops receiving realtime pushes with no indication and no recovery path.

Fix: on the browser `online` event (or via useNetworkStatusEffect) call service.connect() to resume, and have connect() reset reconnectAttempts (or call resetReconnectAttempts()) so a fresh attempt budget is granted; optionally surface the `connection:max-retries-exceeded` state in WebSocketContext so the UI can offer a manual reconnect. Net-new — no prior ppt-web-core finding covered the reconnect give-up / resume lifecycle.
